newsitem.title: USA: CSCE to mull changes in coffee contracts - Bowe.
newsitem.headline: CSCE to mull changes in coffee contracts - Bowe.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) will consider some changes to its coffee contracts, including flexible options and cutting the size of the contract, exchange president Jim Bowe said on Sunday.

"One of the biggest things for coffee options and coffee futures is reducing the size of the contracts for a more efficient market," Bowe said. "It might cause costs to go up, but it would be an easier vehicle to trade and improve market liquidity. The efficiencies would offset costs."
One CSCE coffee contract represents 37,500 pounds -- or some 250 60-kg bags -- of arabica coffee, a large contract particularly for the specialty coffee market, he noted.
Bowe was speaking to members of the coffee trade attending the Specialty Coffee Association of America's three-day conference and exhibition in New Orleans.

Additionally, Bowe said the exchange is looking at flexible options for both coffee and cocoa by the end of 1997. Flexible options, which the CSCE plans to implement in sugar in July, would allow traders to specify strike prices and expiration dates. Currently, the exchange has a limited number of set strike prices and a single expiration date for each options contract.
"With flexible options you could come in and negotiate the terms of the options," Bowe said.
"The exchange will continue to try to make the its contracts more tradable," he added.
